name: Ownership-based attentional bias
fact: Ownership of an object leads to prioritized processing and responses, as evidenced by a reliable change in the point of subjective simultaneity (PSS) in temporal order judgements.
boundary: Behavioral attention and temporal order judgment tasks

provenance.title: I before U: Temporal order judgements reveal bias for self-owned objects
provenance.quote_or_locus: The results indicated a reliable change in the point of subjective simultaneity (PSS) in favour of their own mug

provenance.title: I before U: Temporal order judgements reveal bias for self-owned objects
provenance.quote_or_locus: These findings suggest that ownership, beyond mere-touch, mere-choice, or familiarity, leads to prioritised processing and responses
